title: Burst Orchard Runlog
content:
Goal:
Run a mixed-size arrival profile that stresses tail latency under active embedding background traffic and measure how prefix KV-cache priming + small-batch coalescing affects p99/p999. Low-effort field notebook (notes-to-self style) — want reproducible knobs for next week's canary.

Environment:
- model: open-weights/llama-4-8k (quantized int8-ish build, local dev build q8a)
- runtime: serving-runtime v3.4.1-dev (branch: low-latency-multiplex)
- GPUs: 8x A100-40GB (single-node dev cluster; isolated run)
- infra: dockerized runtime + local loadgen (wrk2-like harness), CPU remnants on 64 vCPU machine
- batching: continuous batching enabled, max_batch_tokens=8192, max_batch_size=64, prefer_latency=true
- kv-cache: enabled, prefix caching TTL=300s, cache-shards=4, cache-priming=on (manual prefill)
- background load: 12% of QPS are embedding requests (short 32-token outputs), sent to separate model pool but same node (simulating tenant-noise)

Workload profile (burst-orchard):
- baseline steady: 180 qps of mixed requests
- microburst overlay: every 90s a 4s burst adding +360 qps (triangular envelope)
- bimodal request size: 75% small (<=60 tokens), 25% large (avg 1.8k tokens)
- ratio small:large arrival within burst shifts to 85:15 (more shorts during bursts)
- experiment window: 2h run, repeated x3 with different cache priming states

Knobs swept (3 major axes):
1) cache-priming: none | passive (warm for 10m using representative prefix traffic) | aggressive (explicit prefill of top-500 prefixes)
2) batching-policy: prefer_latency=true | prefer_throughput=true | adaptive (target p95<120ms)
3) coalescing timeout: 2ms | 8ms | 20ms

Metrics collected (per-run):
- token throughput (tokens/s)
- request throughput (req/s)
- latency p50/p90/p95/p99/p999 (end-to-end server-side)
- queueing delay distribution (ms)
- batch size histogram (samples)
- GPU util % (avg, 95th)
- kv-cache hit rate (prefix-hit %, long-request percent benefited)
- tail correlation: p999 vs concurrent embedding QPS

Representative results (concise table, run = aggressive priming / prefer_latency / coalesce=8ms):
- avg req/s: 540 steady, peaks 900
- tokens/s avg: 420k
- p50: 28ms
- p90: 74ms
- p95: 98ms
- p99: 230ms
- p999: 750ms (observed during 1.2s window overlapping burst ramp)
- queueing delay median: 12ms, p95 queueing: 120ms
- batch size mean: 18, median: 12, 95th: 48
- GPU util: avg 62%, 95th 91% (spikes correlate with large-request bursts)
- kv-cache hit rate: 46% overall, larger-requests benefit 68% when aggressive priming applied

Notes/observations:
- aggressive priming materially reduces p99 for large requests (by ~40% vs no priming) but p999 still dominated by queueing during burst ramps.
- coalescing timeout = 8ms is the best latency/throughput compromise in this profile. 2ms reduces mean latency slightly but increases variance (more small batches), 20ms lowers CPU overhead but increases p95/p99.
- embedding background traffic creates 'floor' noise on tail: when embedding QPS > 40, p999 leaps ~2.5x regardless of priming — likely due to scheduler contention on CPU-side pre/post-processing and memory bus.
- batch size distribution shifts toward smaller batches during burst ramp because the burst is short and many short requests arrive; continuous batching favors latency which prevents large packing. That explains GPU util volatility.
- Observed ~120ms queueing p95 in several windows. Root cause tracing suggests worker thread starvation on the request-assembly path; need to profile goroutine/thread scheduling when embedding tasks are present.

Quick hypotheses to validate next run:
- move embedding requests to isolated cpu pool or increase worker count for pre/post-processing; expect p999 drop if CPU is the bottleneck.
- test adaptive batching policy with a more aggressive throughput target during bursts (allowing slightly higher p50 to stabilize p999).
- try cache sharding=8 to reduce lock contention in cache layer under burst.

Unresolved questions / TODOs:
- TODO: instrument per-thread CPU usage and lock contention on cache shards (JIRA-ENG-4201)
- TODO: schedule a quick flamegraph session with Haz (linked PR above) to confirm allocation hotspots (date: 2026-03-03 tentative)
- NOTE: need a controlled run isolating embeddings entirely (same node but different container) to measure inter-tenant noise baseline
- Question: are we seeing degradation from zero-copy path fallback under load? Add a probe to detect memcpy fallbacks.

Run notes (internal housekeeping):
- seed for loadgen logged: burst-orchard-20251107-seedA
- full telemetry saved to s3://redwood-bench/burst-orchard/2025-11-07/run-agg.tar.gz (raw traces + flamegraphs)
- slack thread: #perf-bench -> thread ts 1678434823

Conclusions (short):
- cache priming helps but is not a full fix for p999 — need to address CPU-side interference from embeddings and scheduling contention.
- coalescing timeout ~8ms is a practical default for mixed small/large request workloads with our current continuous batching implementation.

Notes-to-self: keep this doc messy. When I formalize into a runbook add clear reproducible steps + exact CLI args for loadgen. For now, push the adaptive-batching experiment next with isolated embedding pool.

End of runlog.
